advice: Experiment: test cache-set effects by changing only the existing 64 KiB per-row scratch stride in the LIBXSMM path from 512 floats (2048 bytes) to 544 floats (2176 bytes), updating every row address and the full allocation size consistently. Keep each row's 512 logical values, FP32 arithmetic, tiling, ABI, and streaming transitions unchanged. Hypothesis: the changed row spacing may reduce cache-set conflicts for scratch traffic on the M4 Pro. This is unverified. Compare against fresh paired controls, with allocation, packing, and all scratch traffic inside gemm. Check bounds, row separation, output tolerance, and unchanged general-size and tail behavior.
risks: The supplied evidence does not establish cache-set mapping or that the reference path has scratch rows accessed in a way that benefits from this padding. The larger allocation and altered access pattern may add cache/TLB pressure or address errors. Measure full-call cost and correctness before drawing conclusions; do not infer causality from noisy results.
